Definition: of Hebrew origin (H2226); Zara, (i.e. Zerach), an Israelite:--Zara.
BiblicalUsage: Zara is the Zara of Matthew's genealogy, the twin son of Judah by Tamar. Matthew 1:3 says, "And Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar." The Greek spelling in Matthew puts the accent on the first syllable, while this entry puts it on the last, which is why the word does not resolve by direct lemma, yet he is Zerach, the brother of Pharez, named in the line that leads to Christ.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe it matters that Matthew names Zara at all, because a child of Tamar's tangled story stands in the genealogy of Jesus, which tells me no family line is too broken for God to use.
